candidates.claim: Permission props are named `canDelete` instead of `can<Verb><Noun>` (canDeleteSecret / canDeleteContainer / canDeleteOrder), in the row and list-container props of all three resources.
candidates.evidence: Quick Reject: "Permission prop not named `can<Verb><Noun>`"; B.8: "Boolean permission props must be named can<Verb><Noun> (e.g., canDeleteFlavor  etc)". Code: `canDelete: boolean`. Same in ContainerTableRow.tsx:15, OrderTableRow.tsx:15 and the three *ListContainer.tsx:12.

candidates.claim: Row action menus use `<PopupMenu>` without a `PopupMenuToggle` trigger, so the default toggle is used with no `<Button icon="moreVert" aria-label>`; the icon-only trigger has no accessible label.
candidates.evidence: Quick Reject: "`PopupMenu` without `PopupMenuToggle` as trigger"; B.14: "Context menus must use <PopupMenuToggle as=\"div\"><Button icon=\"moreVert\" /></PopupMenuToggle>". Code: `<PopupMenu><PopupMenuOptions> etc`. Same in ContainerTableRow.tsx:34 and OrderTableRow.tsx:33.
candidates.precedent: Network floating IP / security group views import PopupMenuToggle.

candidates.claim: Delete menu item is neither labelled with the entity nor separated by a divider from the other item (single-entity menu): labels are `Delete` / `Show Details` rather than `Delete Secret` / `Show Secret Details`, and there is no `PopupMenuSectionSeparator` before Delete.
candidates.evidence: B.18: "Single-entity menus  etc: separate the Delete action from the rest with a divider." and "Include the referenced entity in labels". Code: `{canDelete && <PopupMenuItem label={t`Delete`}  etc/>}` directly after `Show Details`. Same in Container/Order rows (line 37/36).

candidates.claim: Delete modals put the object name/ID in the title (`Delete Secret "${secretName}"`, `Delete Order "${orderId}"`) and the confirm label is a bare `Delete` / `Deleting...`; the standard says the object goes in the body and the confirm label should be verb + object type. The body doesn't name the entity at all (container/secret), and the order modal title shows a raw UUID.
candidates.evidence: B.5: "Put the object name in the body, not the title.  etc Reference the affected entity by name/identifier in the body"; "Confirm labels: prefer verb + object type: Delete Image". Code: title={t`Delete Secret "${secretName}"`}, body `This action cannot be undone. The secret will be permanently deleted.` Same at ContainerModals.tsx:109, OrderModals.tsx:125.

candidates.claim: None of the six modals pass `disableCloseButton` while the mutation is pending, so the close-X stays active and the user can dismiss the modal mid-request, while Cancel is disabled (they must be disabled together).
candidates.evidence: Quick Reject: "Modal without `disableCancelButton` / `disableCloseButton` during async operations"; B.5: "disable close-X and Cancel together". Code has `disableCancelButton={deleteMutation.isPending}` only. Same in SecretModals.tsx:60, ContainerModals.tsx:50/116, OrderModals.tsx:58/132.

candidates.claim: The create modals mutate with no form validation and no inline errors: the confirm button is only disabled while pending. Bit Length is parsed with parseInt (NaN on empty), Algorithm may be empty, and fields are not marked required. Validation errors on the server show only as a Message at form top.
candidates.evidence: B.11 Reject: "any form that mutates without validation"; B.5: "keep the primary/confirm button disabled while any required field is empty or any field fails validation". Code: `meta: { algorithm, bit_length: parseInt(bitLength, 10) }`, `disableConfirmButton={createMutation.isPending}`; no @tanstack/react-form / zod used. Secret and container create modals use useState with no validator at all.
candidates.discussion: Copilot thread on OrderModals.tsx:52 (bit length validation).

candidates.claim: The create modals do not follow the form standard (state in `useState` instead of @tanstack/react-form + Zod, no `autoFocus` on the primary input, inputs are not `disabled` while the mutation is in flight, no `required` markers).
candidates.evidence: B.11: "Preferred: @tanstack/react-form with Zod schema validators", "`autoFocus` on the primary input. `disabled={isMutating}` on all inputs during in-flight mutations." Code: `const [name, setName] = useState("")`  etc TextInput has no autoFocus/disabled.

candidates.claim: Create/delete success is silent: no toast is shown for create or delete of secrets, containers or orders; the modal just closes. The standard requires a confirming toast delegated to a `*ToastNotifications` helper for CRUD actions.
candidates.evidence: B.16 table: "CRUD action confirmed (create, delete, update) | toast (transient)"; B.10: "All toast messages must be extracted to a dedicated <Resource>ToastNotifications.tsx"; B.11: "(modal) close and show a confirming toast". grep of the PR diff finds no `toast` and no *ToastNotifications file. onSuccess only calls invalidate()/onClose().

candidates.claim: Row/list sort control is built from raw `Select` + `SortButton` instead of the required `SortInput` from `@/client/components/ListToolbar/SortInput`; Zone 1 is also `distribution="end"` rather than `"between"`.
candidates.evidence: B.1 table: "Sort control | SortInput from @/client/components/ListToolbar/SortInput"; B.2: "Sort controls (SortInput) + primary action Button  etc distribution=\"between\"". Code uses `<Select label="Sort by"  etc>` + `<SortButton  etc/>` in `<Stack distribution="end"  etc className="jn:pb-2">`. Same in OrdersList.tsx:66. Containers list has no sort control at all although the PR body advertises sort for the lists.

candidates.claim: The permission-denied state for the list pages is rendered inline as a non-page-level warning `Message` with hardcoded English and no `mb-4`, instead of a 403 page-level error with an info `Message`; the copy also differs from the recommended 403 text.
candidates.evidence: B.6 Reject: "a 401/403 handled inline instead of via redirect / page-level info Message"; 403 row: "plus an info Message explaining lack of access". Code: `<Message variant="warning">You do not have permission to view secrets.</Message>`. Same ContainersList.tsx:50, OrdersList.tsx:55. B.3 requires `mb-4` on Message banners.
candidates.precedent: Network lists use a Message for the same case ("You do not have permission to view security groups" in messages.po), so this may be accepted locally.

candidates.claim: Reveal Payload button, secret detail and the other detail routes do not check any permission (`key-manager:secrets:payload` / `get`); the control is rendered functional before permissions are known (not fail-closed).
candidates.evidence: Quick Reject: "UI control shown before permissions are resolved (not fail-closed)"; B.7/B.8: "Never optimistically show actions before permissions resolve." Code: `<Button variant="subdued" onClick={handleRevealPayload} disabled={payloadFetching}>`; usePermissions is never imported in the *DetailsView files. The `payload` permission is defined in usePermissions.ts:6 and the policy but unused.

candidates.claim: Detail data is fetched in the component twice (route component and *DetailsView both call the same getX.useQuery) rather than in the route `loader`; the route has no loader, and the breadcrumb is set from a separately fetched copy.
candidates.evidence: A.3: "Data critical for rendering a page must be fetched via the route's loader function rather than loading it inside the component body." and (task) data the loader already fetched is not fetched again. Code: `$containerId.tsx:19 trpcReact.keyManager.getContainer.useQuery( etc)` and `ContainerDetailsView.tsx:31 trpcReact.keyManager.getContainer.useQuery( etc)`. Same for $secretId.tsx:19 / SecretDetailsView.tsx:24 and $orderId.tsx:19 / OrderDetailsView.tsx:22. B.7 allows tRPC useQuery, so severity is a judgement call.

candidates.claim: Files do not follow the B.12 naming table: the modal files bundle two modals each (`SecretModals.tsx`, `ContainerModals.tsx`, `OrderModals.tsx` instead of `CreateSecretModal.tsx` / `DeleteSecretModal.tsx`), the hook file is a generic `usePermissions.ts` instead of `useKeyManagerPermissions.ts`, and `utils.ts` / `constants.ts` are generic names.
candidates.evidence: B.12: "Modal | <Verb><Resource>Modal.tsx"; "Hook | use<PascalCase>.ts (useCephPermissions.ts)"; Reject: "generic names (Modal.tsx, Table.tsx)"; B.8: "a use<Feature>Permissions(projectId) hook". candidates.claim: Import order and path rules are broken: Juno imports come before `@lingui` imports (and `useState` after Juno in SecretModals), and `../../-components/...` relative traversal two levels up is used instead of `@/` aliases.
candidates.evidence: B.13: order is react, i18n, tRPC, Juno; "All imports must use @/ path aliases. No relative ../../ traversal beyond one level." Code: SecretModals.tsx imports Juno (l.1-12) then `useState` from react (l.13); key-manager.tsx:2-4 Juno, server, then lingui. `import { uuidFromRef } from "../../-components/utils"` in all *Modals/*TableRow/*DetailsView files and `import { usePermissions } from "../../-components/usePermissions"` in all *List files; secrets/index.tsx:5 `../-components/utils`.

candidates.claim: User-facing strings are not translated: JSX button/placeholder/label literals (`Create Secret`, `Search by name...`, `Sort by`, `Created At`), the permission-denied Messages, and the DataGrid column header arrays in constants.ts (`Name / ID`, `Status`, `Type`, ...) are plain English, so the de locale will show English.
candidates.evidence: B.14: "All user-facing strings must be wrapped in <Trans> or t` etc`" (the review scope says lingui lint covers aurora, but these aren't caught). `export const SECRETS_COLUMNS = ["Name / ID", "Status",  etc]`; SecretsList.tsx:97 `Create Secret`, :105 `placeholder="Search by name etc"`, :84 `label="Sort by"`; `msgid "Name / ID"` and `msgid "Search by name"` are absent from en/messages.po at head (git show | grep).
candidates.precedent: Low priority: out of the stated review scope if lint is assumed to catch it.

candidates.claim: Empty-state wording does not distinguish `no data` from `no filter results`: with an active search the secrets/containers list shows `There are no secrets in this project. Create one to get started.`
candidates.evidence: B.6: "Distinguish empty reasons: 'no data' -> suggest creating; 'no filter results' -> suggest clearing filters." Code shows the same `No Secrets Found` / create body whether or not `search` is set (the list container does not receive `search`). Same in ContainerListContainer.tsx:58, and the empty Create hint is shown even to users without create permission.

candidates.claim: Error states render the raw `error.message` as the Status title (`error?.message ?? t`Failed to Load Secret``), with no retry action or explanatory body.
candidates.evidence: B.6: "Always communicate the state and a possible course of action (retry link where feasible)"; "any empty/broken state without explanatory title/body". Code: `<Status status="error" title={error?.message ?? t`Failed to Load Secrets`} />`; same in all list containers and DetailsViews (e.g. ContainerDetailsView.tsx:37). Detail pages also have no `errorComponent`/403 handling of their own.
